validity.recommendation: Existence, ownership, status, and the length/diameter numbers are all solidly confirmed -- but P4107 is likely mis-structured as a single row. SNGPL's own transmission-segment inventory (Annual Reports 2015-2018, unchanged across 4 consecutive years) lists 'SIDHNAI - FAISALABAD' as FOUR separate table rows by diameter: 18-in/163.58km, 24-in/50.24km, 30-in/53.29km, 36-in/26.42km. GEM split the 18-in line off as its own row (P4106, exact match), then combined the remaining three (24/30/36-in) into ONE row (P4107) with a summed length (50.24+53.29+26.42=129.95km, exact match to GEM's LengthKnown) and a multi-value Diameter field ('24, 30, 36'). Elsewhere in this same roster, GEM does NOT do this for structurally identical cases: the Sui-Multan corridor has FOUR separate PIDs -- P4090 (mainline) plus P4091/P4097/P4098 as 'Loopline I/II/III', each its own row with its own single diameter and length, even though they nominally parallel the same corridor. P4107 groups three non-continuous loop segments (different lengths, not sequential portions of one route) under one PID with a multi-diameter field, which is the pattern GEM normally reserves for a single continuous route whose pipe diameter changes along its length (e.g. P4019 Dadu-Malir-Karachi, dia='20, 18'), not for parallel/looped segments. Recommend either (a) splitting P4107 into three separate loopline rows analogous to Sui-Multan's I/II/III convention, each with its own single diameter and length, or (b) if kept as one row, add a ResearcherNotes entry documenting that the combined 129.95km/24,30,36-in fields represent three distinct SNGPL loop segments, not one continuous pipe of varying diameter -- so a future researcher doesn't misread it as the latter.
validity.researcher_notes: gem.wiki returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) for this row's own page and for wiki_citations.json harvest, so there was no existing sourced citation to start from -- went straight to open-web/primary-source research per scope guidance. General web search (site search engines largely CAPTCHA'd/blocked automated fetch this session, so used lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/ which worked) for '"Sidhnai-Faisalabad Gas Pipeline II"' returns exactly ONE hit: the GEM wiki page itself -- i.e. no independent web presence under that exact pipeline name, which would be a serious existence red flag on its own. However, 'Sidhnai' and 'Faisalabad' independently point to a real, well-documented SNGPL transmission corridor: SNGPL's own audited Annual Reports (downloaded and pdftotext-verified fresh for AR2016, AR2017, AR2018 -- identical figures across all three, and also present in a locally-cached AR2015) contain a 'TRANSMISSION SYSTEM PIPELINES' inventory table listing 'SIDHNAI - FAISALABAD' with rows: 18-in/163.58km, 24-in/50.24km, 30-in/53.29km, 36-in/26.42km (there is also a separate 'SIDHNAI X-ING - AC-7' 36-in/33.26km row and a separate 'MULTAN - SIDHNAI' set of rows for the corridor on the OTHER side of the Sidhnai crossing -- neither of those appears to be captured under any PID in the 63-row roster I was given, which may be a discovery gap worth flagging separately, out of scope here). GEM's P4106 (Sidhnai-Faisalabad Gas Pipeline, the 'I') matches the 18-in/163.58km row exactly. P4107's LengthKnown (129.95km) is the EXACT sum of the 24+30+36-in rows (50.24+53.29+26.42=129.95), and its Diameter field ('24, 30, 36 in') lists exactly those three diameters -- so the underlying numbers are demonstrably sourced correctly from SNGPL's own data, just combined into one row rather than kept as three. 'Sidhnai' itself is independently corroborated as a real place-name tied to Abdul Hakim: a 2006 PSIG (Pipeline Simulation Interest Group) conference paper by an SNGPL engineer (S.R. Lone) and a UK hydraulics consultant (R.P. Spiers), 'Gas Transmission Development Strategy - a modeling approach' (PSIG 0602), independently describes a 'Sidhnai Crossing on the Ravi River' with parallel 16-in and 30-in pipe (I could not re-locate a live URL for this PDF to cite it formally -- noting it here for context only, not as a citation, per the no-fabricated-URL rule); and a public Facebook page 'Head Sidhnai Official | Abdul Hakim' independently ties the Sidhnai barrage/crossing to the Abdul Hakim locale that GEM records as StartLocation, consistent with GEM's endpoint attribution (also not cited formally -- informal source, mentioned for context only). Net: existence is well confirmed (a named, real SNGPL transmission asset, present unchanged across 4 years of audited annual reports, corroborated by an unrelated engineering conference paper for the place-name), status=operating/Fuel=Gas/PipelineType=transmission are all correct (it's listed as an active line in SNGPL's own transmission-system table), Owner1=SNGPL 100% is self-evidently correct (it is SNGPL's own asset in SNGPL's own asset inventory). The residual concern is purely structural/classification: whether three non-continuous loop segments should be one PID with a multi-value diameter, or three PIDs matching the Sui-Multan precedent.
